meta.note: Good practices were found by web search in October 2026. One-line takeaways are in our own words and based on the page that was read. Items marked as not read were listed from titles only.

sources.title: WOAH Observatory annual report 2022, key findings: PVS Pathway
sources.takeaway: 448 PVS activities in 2006 to 2021 (Africa 208), an analysis of levels of advancement for 43 Members (2016-2021) and signs of decreasing interest in PVS Follow-up and Gap Analysis missions.

sources.title: Overview of the PVS Pathway
sources.takeaway: Four steps (orientation, PVS Evaluation, planning, targeted support) and the tools for each, including PVS Gap Analysis 2.0 and the strategic planning template.

sources.title: The OIE PVS Tool: quick overview of the 45 critical competencies
sources.takeaway: Lists all competencies under the four fundamental components.

sources.title: One Health capacity building (PVS Pathway)
sources.takeaway: Explains IHR-PVS National Bridging Workshops run with FAO and WHO, the four steps, and that PVS experts join JEE missions where PVS missions have taken place.

sources.title: IHR-PVS National Bridging Workshop fact sheet
sources.takeaway: Three-day workshop; 16 joint technical areas; works best after a JEE and before a national action plan; ends in a joint roadmap.

sources.title: Participant handbook, National Bridging Workshop: capitalizing on IHR and PVS (version 7.0)
sources.takeaway: Participant guide for the three-day workshop: seven sessions taking human, animal and environmental health from One Health concepts and a gap review across 16 technical areas to a joint operational roadmap.

sources.title: National Bridging Workshop on the IHR and the OIE PVS Pathway: Kyrgyzstan (Bishkek, 2-4 October 2018)
sources.takeaway: Health and veterinary services agreed a joint roadmap: an intersectoral committee on zoonoses with focal points at oblast and rayon level, a joint surveillance strategy and shared database, harmonised laboratory methods, and joint outbreak response and risk communication.
sources.note: Takeaway based on the report's roadmap section.

sources.title: Report of the National Bridging Workshop on the IHR and the OIE PVS Pathway, Pakistan (Islamabad, 9-11 May 2017)
sources.takeaway: Top priority was a formal One Health coordination mechanism, with One Health hubs at federal, provincial and district level, a harmonised laboratory information system and joint surveillance piloted at district level.
sources.note: Takeaway based on the report's summary.

sources.title: Integrating wildlife health through IHR-PVS National Bridging Workshops
sources.takeaway: Slides showing how a wildlife health session is built into the bridging workshops (more than 60 held so far, each ending in a joint roadmap), using an avian influenza scenario with wild bird die-offs.

sources.title: Independent review of PVS Pathway reports from African Member Countries: final report
sources.authors: Weaver Consulting International, Intiga Consulting, Colibri Consulting (for OIE)
sources.takeaway: Desk review of PVS Evaluation and Follow-up reports: little overall change in levels of advancement across Africa, with persistent gaps in veterinary staffing, laboratory quality assurance, risk analysis, food safety, traceability, veterinary medicines and funding; confidentiality of reports limits their use.

sources.title: Evaluation of the PVS Pathway programme: final report
sources.takeaway: The PVS Pathway is valued but often under-used because reports are not acted on or shared; publishing reports, digitising data and more frequent follow-ups would raise its impact.
